name: Surface-code memory experiment (Stim + PyMatching)
summary: Estimate the logical error rate of a rotated surface-code memory with Stim sampling, PyMatching decoding and a Wilson interval.
description:
Runs a rotated surface-code memory experiment locally. Stim generates the noisy syndrome-extraction circuit for the chosen distance, number of rounds and memory basis, samples detector outcomes, and PyMatching decodes them with minimum-weight perfect matching. The product reports logical failures, the logical error rate and its 95% Wilson score interval; zero observed failures is reported as an upper bound, never as a rate of zero.

For QEC students and researchers who want a correct, seeded baseline for a surface-code memory without assembling Stim and PyMatching themselves. The sampling seed is derived exactly as in the SDK's existing `surface-code-memory-mwpm` benchmark, so the same inputs reproduce the same samples.
useCases: Measure the logical error rate at one distance and physical error rate, with a confidence interval
Compare distances below threshold to see the logical error rate fall
Produce a reproducible MWPM baseline to compare a new decoder against on identical settings

inputs.name: rounds
inputs.description: Syndrome-extraction rounds. null uses d rounds.

inputs.name: physical_error_rate
inputs.description: Depolarizing probability p applied after every Clifford gate.

inputs.name: basis
inputs.description: Memory basis: x prepares and measures the logical X observable, z the logical Z observable.

outputs.name: logical_failures
outputs.description: Shots whose decoded logical observable was wrong.

outputs.name: logical_error_rate
outputs.description: logical_failures / shots (per memory experiment of the given rounds, not per round).

outputs.name: confidence_interval
outputs.description: 95% Wilson score interval: lower, upper, level, method.

outputs.name: is_upper_bound_only
outputs.description: true when no failure was observed; then only the upper bound is meaningful.

outputs.name: decoder_version
outputs.description: Installed PyMatching version that produced the result.

changes: First catalog release, wrapping the SDK's existing Stim + PyMatching surface-code memory experiment.

environment.resources: d=7 with 10^5 shots at p=0.001: ~0.3 s on a 2024 Apple-silicon laptop (measured). Time grows roughly as d^3 x shots; memory holds one byte per detector per shot, and runs needing more than 2 GiB of samples are refused.

example.code:
import json
from ketqat_runner import catalog

record = catalog.run("surface-code-memory@1.0.0", seed=2026, distance=3, physical_error_rate=0.005, shots=2000)
result = record.result
interval = result["confidence_interval"]
print(json.dumps({
    "status": record.status,
    "distance": result["distance"],
    "rounds": result["rounds"],
    "decoder": result["decoder"],
    "observed_failures": result["logical_failures"] > 0,
    "interval_brackets_rate": interval["lower"] <= result["logical_error_rate"] <= interval["upper"],
}))

verified.platform: macOS-27.0.1-arm64-arm-64bit (maintainer run of python/tests/test_catalog_examples.py; not yet run by CI)

sampleResult.summary: d=5, 5 rounds, memory Z at p=0.003: 74 logical failures in 100000 shots, rate 0.00074 with 95% Wilson interval [0.00059, 0.00093].

assumptions: Circuit-level noise: single- and two-qubit depolarizing noise with probability p after every Clifford gate (Stim's after_clifford_depolarization). Measurement, reset and idle errors are not added.
Stabilizer simulation: only Pauli noise is representable.
The decoder sees the detector error model of the same circuit that generated the samples (matched noise model).
scope: Rotated surface code, memory in the X or Z basis, odd distance 3 to 25, 1 to 100 rounds.
Logical error rate per memory experiment with a 95% Wilson score interval.
limitations: One noise model only; real devices have measurement, leakage, crosstalk and coherent errors that this does not include. A rate here is not a hardware prediction.
No threshold is estimated by a single run; sweep distances and rates and compare intervals yourself.
Rates are per experiment of the given number of rounds, not per round.
Exact counts are reproducible for the same seed with the same Stim and PyMatching versions; other versions may sample or decode differently.
Large distances with many shots take minutes; time grows with d^3 x shots, and runs needing more than 2 GiB of detector samples are refused rather than started.
Tested on macOS and Linux only; Windows is untested.

origin.statement: The surface code memory and its decoding by matching follow Dennis, Kitaev, Landahl and Preskill (2002) and Fowler et al. (2012). Circuits are generated and sampled by Stim (Craig Gidney) and decoded by PyMatching (Oscar Higgott and Craig Gidney); both are used unmodified as dependencies. KetQat wrote the integration: parameter handling, seed derivation, Wilson-interval reporting, validation tests and this catalog entry. KetQat did not invent the code, the noise model or the decoder.

validation.description: At p = 0 no logical failure is observed and the result is reported as an upper bound only.
Below threshold (memory Z, p = 0.003, 100000 shots, fixed seed) the d = 5 logical error rate is below the d = 3 rate with disjoint 95% Wilson intervals.
Every result carries a 95% Wilson score interval that brackets the point estimate.
The product reproduces the logical failure count of the SDK's surface-code-memory-mwpm 0.1.0 manifest run at the same distance, rate, seed and shots.
The example code is executed verbatim in a clean virtual environment with only the qec extra installed.
